findings.detail: Canonical pure-bash fence wrote docs/data/cycle-snapshot-08:20.json (16451 B) for NOMINAL tick 08:15 — offset +5 min. findings.detail: chef-intraday claimed a MARKET publish. Verified against market_messages via get_market_message_digest + get_unreviewed_market_messages (persisted DB record, not self-report): id=1214, sent_at 2026-08-24 08:23:06, content matches the claimed FII/FTSE real-estate thesis line for line (VHM RSI 24.5 +2.37%, VIC +4.63%, KDH +3.06% BB breakout, SSI 4bn USD inflow forecast). NOT fabricated. Recorded affirmatively because chef publish claims are the highest-fabrication-history class in this fleet and a verified-true instance is as much a datapoint as a false one.

All THREE of today's chef dishes are mis-attributed in market_messages: ids 1210 (04:20:40), 1212 (06:21:17), 1214 (08:23:06) all carry from_agent='mcp-user', message_type='user_ask_reply'. Correct values would be the chef agent + a dish type. This is NOT a global defect: same table, same day, france-summary id 1211 carries from_agent='france-summary'/message_type='france_summary' and morning-briefing id 1204 is correctly attributed. So the send path used by other producers stamps identity correctly and chef's does not. Previously logged as a 2-id observation (1210/1212 vs correct 1211); today gives a clean same-day triple with a working control in the same minute range. Blast radius: every MARKET-channel quality review (batch_review_market_messages) and any per-agent post attribution is wrong for chef.

chef-intraday wrote both its artifacts and committed NEITHER. docs/agent-memory/notebooks/unified-agent.md is ' M' (modified, uncommitted); docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-08-24-chef-intraday.json is '??' (untracked). Zero chef commits in the 12 min window around the run (git log --since shows only peer-session commits). Its own contract requires commit-mutex notebook persistence. This is a live reproduction of the 'organic per-cycle uncommitted deliverables' population from the chef-strand two-population finding — and note it is the SAME shape as the coverage-state.json strand pinned this morning: the agent genuinely does the write, reports it truthfully, and the durability step silently does not happen. The return text does not claim a commit, so nothing in the report is false; the absence is what has to be caught.

Both naming conventions co-exist for 2026-08-24 from the same agent: unified-agent-synthesis-2026-08-24-chef-intraday.json (4114 B, 08:24Z, this cycle) and unified-agent-synthesis-2026-08-24-intraday.json (3163 B, 06:21Z, the earlier intraday cycle). Same agent, same slot family, same day, two filenames. Any consumer globbing one pattern silently misses the other. BOTH are untracked in git, so the split is invisible to anything reading from a commit. Carried finding, now with a same-day control pair rather than a cross-day inference.

docs/agent-memory/notebooks/unified-agent.md carries TWO identical '## Prior cycles' headings (lines 66 and 70), and today's two cycles wrote two different section shapes: line 74 '## 2026-08-24 - Intraday Cycle (06:13 UTC)' vs line 86 '## Cycle 2026-08-24 08:13 UTC (chef-intraday)'. Older entries use a third shape, '## Session: <date> (evening 19:45 UTC)'. A drop-oldest-'## '-section pruner cannot behave predictably against duplicate keys and heterogeneous shapes - this is the same structural class as FIX-ALERT-COMMANDER-NOTEBOOK-SINGLE-BLOB-UNPRUNABLE (2026-07-29), which alert-commander fixed by mandating exactly one '## c<NNN>' shape per cycle. unified-agent never got that treatment.
findings.evidence: grep -n '^## ' docs/agent-memory/notebooks/unified-agent.md -> 7 headings, 3 distinct shapes, '## Prior cycles' x2

It has crossed from internal telemetry into user-facing investment commentary, where it is being given as the REASON for a recommendation. The agent declined to escalate its push rejection on the premise it is 'the same, already-tracked P0 BACKLOG row'. The pre-push gate names THREE offenders; the board covers ONE. Measured per-file against task_board only: pushBctcLayoutHandler.ts -> backlog[491] (covers the size defect, correct). ocr_gateway.py -> review[25] FIX-OCRGATEWAY-INFLIGHT-BOOKKEEPING-DIVERGES-OS-TRUTH (in-flight bookkeeping, NOT line count) + backlog[233] (MD-table OCR routing, not size) = ZERO size rows. tasksMdJanitorJob.ts -> backlog[411] (task_kind enum), review[7] (auditor D4 whitelist), done_verified[48] (tool registration) = ZERO size rows, and it is the LARGEST overshoot at 1012L vs 996L upper. So one correct row was treated as coverage for a three-file blocker. This is a RECURRENCE of an already-named finding: SIZELINT-COVERAGE-STILL-OPEN-AFTER-FALSE-SUPPRESSION and SIZELINT-GATE-NAMES-3-OFFENDERS-BOARD-COVERS-1 both already sit in pending_triage_inbox. The dedup lesson the agent applied is correct in kind and wrong in scope: verify coverage per OFFENDER, not per blocker-name.

Return states 'My notebook commit sits locally on main, one commit ahead of origin/main, and will ride along once the gate clears.' Measured: git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD = 0 / 203. HEAD is 203 commits ahead, not 1. Baseline recorded earlier today was 192, so the strand is still growing (+11). The understatement matters because it reframes a multi-day fleet-wide push outage as a single deferred commit awaiting a routine clear - which is exactly the reading that keeps a P0 from being escalated. The agent's own commit riding along is true; the branch state around it is not.

Re-measured this tick: all three offenders are CLEAN in the worktree and each has exactly 1 commit inside origin/main..HEAD. Therefore backlog[481] FIX-SIZELINT-PREPUSH-SCANS-WORKING-TREE-NOT-PUSH-RANGE, if implemented, releases ZERO commits - a push-range-scoped scan still sees all three files. The load-bearing blocker is coverage (two offenders with no size row), not scan scope. Second independent confirmation.

New downstream consequence of the cycle-snapshot wall-clock naming defect. Slot alert-commander-market fired for nominal tick 2026-08-24T08:15:00Z. Step 4.7 wrote the snapshot as cycle-snapshot-08:20.json (FILE_TICK=date -u +%H:%M, +5 offset). The agent found that file and labelled its notebook section '## c227 ... tick=08:20'. Its three preceding sections all carry nominal ticks (c224 tick=07:45, c225 tick=08:00, c226 tick=08:00) because no snapshot existed those cycles and they fell back to nominal. So the defect is not confined to silent promotion failure inside emit_pressure_state - when a snapshot IS present, the consumer inherits the wall-clock name and writes a WRONG tick id into a permanent, committed agent record. Anyone correlating notebook cycles to dispatch ticks after the fact gets a 5-minute skew that appears only on cycles where the snapshot worked.

Notebook c227 records 'CYCLE_SNAPSHOT hit tick=08:20 (1min fresh)'. Measured: snapshot created_at=2026-08-24T08:20:18Z, c227 section header timestamp 2026-08-24T08:24:46Z = 4.5 min apart. Consistent with age-computed-at-READ-time paired with a WRITE-time section header, which is internally coherent but undocumented and unlabelled - a reader cannot tell 1min-at-read from 1min-at-write. Fourth datapoint on this annotation class. Not re-escalated; recorded so the convention gets pinned rather than re-discovered.

c227 numbered and pruned cleanly with no collision. This is NOT evidence the missing read-then-write mutex is harmless: only alert-commander-market fired at 08:15Z (alert-commander-critical is */4h and did not co-fire). The 08:00Z collision required BOTH slots in the same wall-clock minute. A single-slot tick cannot exercise the race by construction. The remedy (port market-watcher-notebook:main shape - claim BEFORE the read, hold THROUGH the commit) remains open regardless of this clean run.
